meta.title: DNS Mesh Protocol
meta.description: An open protocol for end-to-end encrypted messages delivered over DNS. No central server, no app store, no gatekeeper.

hero.title: Encrypted mail, delivered by the same lookup that finds google.com.
hero.lede: DNS Mesh moves end-to-end encrypted messages between two people over plain DNS — no relay company, no app store, no account to create.

anchor.label: mental model
anchor.text: Think of it as federated email, except it runs on DNS instead of SMTP.

i.title: Identity
i.body: A name in DNS, not in an app store. Public TXT records under the recipient’s domain hold the long-term Ed25519 and X25519 keys.

ii.title: Mailbox slots
ii.body: Forward-secret prekeys advertised the same way. Anyone on the public DNS chain can fetch them; only the holder can answer.

iii.title: Ciphertext
iii.body: Chunked, signed via RFC 8945 TSIG, written with RFC 2136 DNS UPDATE. The recursive chain only ever sees opaque bytes.

prose.title: Reads are open. Writes are signed.
prose.p1: That asymmetry is what removes the gatekeeper. Anyone, on any network, can resolve any user’s identity, mailbox slots, and chunks — the records are public TXT entries served by ordinary DNS. Mutations, on the other hand, are RFC 2136 DNS UPDATE packets signed with an RFC 8945 TSIG key issued per user.
prose.p2: One HTTPS call mints the key on first registration; after that, no HTTPS hop is involved in publishing identity, refreshing prekeys, or delivering chunks. Every node in the federation accepts those updates from any user whose key it knows about, which means no single node is canonical and none of them can hold a conversation hostage.

try.title: Five minutes against the public node.
try.intro: The reference node at dnsmesh.io is open registration and serves the bootstrap-seed and claim-provider roles other nodes default to. Self-hosting gets the same capabilities — both modes interoperate over DNS, because the wire is the contract.

warn.label: notice
warn.lead: The protocol is not yet audited.
warn.body: Wire format, federation, identity and key rotation, and the formal spec have all shipped, but the cryptographic audit hasn’t. Don’t route confidentiality-critical traffic through DMP yet. Read
warn.tail: before you trust this with anything that matters.
